description: to remove The component allows to setup basic form props and wraps all Form items which are inside.

onSubmit.description: Function could be synchronous or asynchronous and it is run after all validations completed without error after submitting form. Parameters: event [object] - object with value as event.data.value . The value is an object containing values from all nested input components, using "input name -> input value" mapping. This property is intended to be passed from the parent component and should generally be provided by it. Example: onSubmit={async (e) => { return await Calls.buyProduct(e.data.value); }}

submitUri.description: to remove The primary endpoint to which form data is submitted upon form completion.

submitDataMap.description: to remove Specifies map how should be form data submit. It is specified in a form of an object where each key is a name of a key from the form data. Using a dot notation, the source key can even inserted as a full path to a key of an object, which is nested inside of another object in form data. A value of each key specifies the name of a property to which the given data should be sent. Example: submitDataMap={{ "name": "user.fullName", "email": "user.email" }}

loadUri.description: to remove This property specifies the endpoint from which initial data is loaded to populate form input fields.

loadData.description: to remove Contains data for initial load. Only when loadUri is filled. Example: loadData={{ "id": "01234..." }}

loadDataMap.description: to remove Specifies map how should be data translate upon load. It is specified in a form of an object where each key is a name of a key from the loaded data. Using a dot notation, the source key can even inserted as a full path to a key of an object, which is nested inside of another object in loaded data. A value of each key specifies the name of a property to which the given data should be sent. Example: loadDataMap={{ "nextWeekDate": "deliveryDate" }}

tabList.description: This property is only used in edit mode (extend tabList in edit modal). Defines items in the left menu. The array's items must be either template names or objects with the following structure: template (string) - instead of building a custom tab and its content, we can use a selection of prebuilt tab templates. Existing templates can be found at Tab templates section of this book. label (node - lsi) - define label for each tab layout (sizeOf(string)) - a css grid-template-areas like layout setup that is used to position individual prop inputs from propInputMap inside a grid layout feature a possibility to insert also a separator (line) component - using a key word - within the layout specification. For usage other component then default seprator, there is option to define custom component in prop propInputMap with key - columns (sizeOf(string)) - defines number and sizing of columns for the tab's content. E.g. columns: { m: "repeat(4, 1fr)" } - results in 4 columns each taking 25% of the content container for screensizes [m, l, xl] while there will be only 1 column for screensizes [xs, s]. propInputMap (object) - same as the root propInputMap but this one takes priority allowing us to overwrite some general prop input settings in root propInputMap . Shallow merge is used to merge these two maps and also the same technique is used for merging values of passed property props . icon (icon) - name of an icon representing the edit section. info (node) - a description of the edit section (default will be automatically generated if not defined). hiddenInputList ([string]) - list of prop names that are not in the layout key because they are nested in another component. maxHeight (unit - "auto") - the key defines the max height of the active tab content. visible (bool) - allows to hide current tab. Default value is true. Example: tabList={["advanced"]} or tabList={[{ template: "advanced", label: "Custom label", propInputMap: { autoComplete: { props: { info: "..." } } } }]} or tabList={[{ label: { en: "Submit" }, layout: { xs: `header, -, headerType, level, headerSeparator`, m: `header header header, - - -, headerType level level, headerSeparator headerSeparator headerSeparator` }, columns: { m: "repeat(3, 1fr) } }]}

propInputMap.description: This property is only used in edit mode (extend tabList in edit modal). Includes object representation of input for editing a prop. The objects in the map must have the following structure: "<propName>" (object) component (string) - defines which Uu5Forms or custom component will be used for editing the prop. E.g. component: "Uu5Forms.FormSwitchSelect" props (object) - defines props of component above (object) - defines props of component above propMap (object) - this key is suitable for multiple input. Multiple input contains multiple inputs and needs to get multiple values from EditModal props. The keys define the names of the props for the multiple input. Values define the names of the props in EditModal. Example: propInputMap={{ info: { component: Uu5Forms.FormTextArea, props: {label: { en: "Info" },autoResize: true,} }, }} This root propInputMap takes priority allowing us to overwrite some general prop input settings in a system propInputMap . Shallow merge is used to merge these two maps and also the same technique is used for merging values of passed property props . There is a list of basic pre-made prop input templates (from Uu5Editing) that can be used in tabList via layout key that do not need to be specified in propInputMap unless you wish to override some of their properties. There is also a list of specific pre-made prop input templates for this Form component. Be carefull with overrading specific input templates because these templates are used in other Form tabs. Example of colorScheme prop input template with a custom selection of color palettes it should display: propInputMap={{ colorScheme: { props: {valueList: ["building", "basic"]}, }, }}

itemList.description: A complete list of available items to be displayed by the component before the user starts inputting characters in the search field. Each item is defined as an object with the following keys: value (any) - serves as an unique identifier of the item which, for example, allows the component to determine, which of the items are currently selected. children (node - lsi) - what the item will be displayed as (component, text). If not defined, value is used. icon (icon) - name of an icon to be displayed at the item's left side. iconRight (icon) - name of an icon to be display at the item's right side. disabled (bool) - allows to disable an item heading (bool) - Renders a visually modified MenuItem that is suitable as a header for other MenuItems displayed below it. If the value set to undefined and the children key is undefined , the cross to remove the selection displays on the left side. This item will not display in the popover. Example: itemList={[ {value: "apple"}, {value: "banana", children: "Banana"}, {value: "lemon", children: <Uu5Elements.Badge>Lemon</Uu5Elements.Badge>}]}

description: @since 2.18.0 The editing table renders the data set. The table can copy and paste from/to Excel, basic sorting and data formatting.

data.description: This prop defines the list of data cells to render. Data can also contain styles of cell or row. @since 2.20.0 Row data can also contain headerCells flag (whether cells in this row are styled as header cells). Example: ( only data) data={[["John", "Doe"], [...data of next row]} (data and styles on the whole row) data={[ { value: ["John", "Doe"], style: { significance: "distinct", colorScheme: "blue", horizontalAlignment: "center" }, headerCells: true } {...data of next row}, }]} (data and styles on the cell) data={[ [{ value: "John", style: { significance: "distinct", colorScheme: "blue" } }, "Doe"], [...data of next row], ]} (data and styles on the whole row and styles on the cell) data={[ { value: [{ value: "John", style: { significance: "distinct", colorScheme: "blue" } }, "Doe"], style: { fontSize: 24 } }, {...data of next row}, ]}

columnList.description: This prop defines column settings. Each object defines properties for one column. Columns are shown in the same order as placed in this array. Click here for the available keys for column settings. Example: columnList={[ { header: "Id", maxWidth: "xs", ... }, { header: "Orders", footer: "Total", ... }, ]}

height.description: This prop defines a fixed height of the component. If it is not entered, it will render all the items and will be as high as all its rows. Example: height={200}

maxHeight.description: This prop defines the maximum height of the component. Example: maxHeight={400}

hideHeader.description: This prop defines whether the header row should be hidden. Example: hideHeader={true}

hideFooter.description: This prop defines whether the footer row should be hidden. Example: hideFooter={true}

tileBreakpoint.description: The prop defines the screen size from which a Tile view will be display. Tile view is more compact and is optimized for mobile devices. Example: tileBreakpoint="none"

theme.description: This prop defines a theme. Each theme has different predefined styles - cell background and borders. The appearance of the component can be modified using other props (e.g. colorScheme , significance , borderWidth etc.) Example: theme="horizontal-b"

colorScheme.description: This prop defines colored appearance the whole component. Color defining semantic sense throughout the information hierarchy. Available values are defined in PropTypes as building and basic colors. Example: colorScheme="green"

significance.description: This prop defines significance that differentiates styling according to its visibility or visual expression throughout the interface. Example: significance="highlighted"

borderColorScheme.description: This prop defines a border color for a certain border type. Available border types are defined by keys: horizontal , vertical , outside , header and footer . Available values of colorScheme are defined in PropTypes as building and basic colors. Example: borderColorScheme={{ vertical: "blue", horizontal: "red", outside: "pink" }}

borderWidth.description: This prop defines a border width for a certain border type. Available border types are defined by keys: horizontal , vertical , outside , header and footer . Available values of widths are none , thin and strong . Example: borderWidth={{ vertical: "none", horizontal: "thin", outside: "strong" }}

virtualization.description: This prop d efines whether the component will virtualize its data. Virtualization improves performance of the page by only rendering the data that are in the viewport of the page. Disabling will cause the entire table to render at once, which may worsen performance depending on the content, but it allows searching using Ctrl(Cmd)+F. Available values of this prop are: undefined - virtualization is automatically applied for more than 100 rows in data prop. "none" - no virtualization. "row" - virtualization of rows. "table" - virtualization of rows and columns Example: virtualization="row"

exportTypeList.description: This prop defines the list of allowed formats for exporting table data. Available formats are json , xls and csv . If the list is empty, export is disabled. Example: exportTypeList={["json", "xls"]}

spacing.description: This prop defines padding in the cells. The prop value can be defined by any unit , number or adaptive size ( a , b , c or d ). Example: spacing=8 spacing="8px" spacing="8px 16px" spacing="a b c" spacing="8px 12px 16px 18px" spacing="xs: 8px; m: 16px; l: 18px"

padding.description: This prop defines the space size only on the left and right side of the row (space between Table border and first or last cell). The prop value can be defined by any unit , number or adaptive size ( a , b , c or d ). Example: padding=8 padding="8px" padding="b" padding="xs: 8px; m: 16px; l: 18px"

margin.description: This prop defines the size of the space around the component. The prop value can be defined by any unit , number or adaptive size ( a , b , c or d ). Example: margin=8 margin="8px" margin="8px 16px" margin="a b c" margin="8px 12px 16px 18px" margin="xs: 8px; m: 16px; l: 18px"

sortable.description: This prop defines whether sorting is enabled on all columns (except columns that have the type set to component ). Example: sortable={false}

headerStyle.description: This prop defines styles for all header cells. Click here for the available keys for style settings. Example: headerStyle={{ colorScheme: "green", bold: true, fontSize: "18px", ... }}

footerStyle.description: This prop defines styles for all footer cells. Click here for the available keys for style settings. Example: footerStyle={{ colorScheme: "green", italic: true, horizontalAlignment: "center", ... }}

stripedRows.description: This prop allows to set different color shade on the odd and even rows. The default value depends on the selected theme . Example: stripedRows={false}

stickyHeader.description: This prop defines whether the header should stick to the top of its nearest scrolling ancestor. Traditionally this means that if any part of the Table is visible, then the header will be, too. Example: stickyHeader={false}

stickyFooter.description: This prop defines whether the footer should stick to the bottom of its nearest scrolling ancestor. Traditionally this means that if any part of the Table is visible, then the footer will be, too. Example: stickyFooter={false}

borderRadius.description: This prop defines rounded corners on the component. Border radius could be one of the defined values in PropTypes .borderRadius (except "full"). The default value is set based on the selected the theme prop. Example: borderRadius="moderate"

description: @since 2.4.0 Component is used to display an image or its thumbnail.

margin.description: The prop defines the size of the space around the component. Example: margin={8} or margin="8px" or margin="8px 16px" margin="8px 12px 16px" or margin="8px 12px 16px 18px"

loadingContent.description: This content is rendered while image is loading. Image component creates placeholder by passed width, height and aspectRatio and render loadingContent at the center of the placeholder.

thumbnailSrc.description: Url source of thumbnail image. Image from set url is displayed in the content and props.src is used and rendered only in the displayed lightbox.

fit.description: cover - the image is centered and shrinked to cover the whole area preserving its own aspect ratio, merely centered and possibly clipped in the other dimension if it overflows. contain - Image is centered and scaled to maintain its aspect ratio while fitting the area. @since 2.4.0 contain-background - Image is centered and scaled to maintain its aspect ratio while fitting the area and around the image is a blurred background filling the rest of the area . fill - The entire image will completely fill the box. If the object's aspect ratio does not match the aspect ratio of its box, then the object will be stretched to fit. To be able to use fit property, there has to be defined width and height property.

effect.description: Effect that shows on hover on thumbnail. Supported effects: none , zoom , grayscale , blur , invert , tilt , morph , sepia .

width.description: Required thumbnail image width (px). The second dimension is calculated to preserve the aspect ratios of the image.

height.description: Required thumbnail height (px). The second dimension is calculated to preserve the aspect ratios of the image.

lightbox.description: Lightbox is interface for displaying images with several functions as zoom, fullscreen, autoplay or browsing through the images with the same lightbox. Value can be bool, which sets if the component should be registered to the gobal lightbox (all components with lightbox={true} on the same page). The string value is used to register component to a local lightbox, where the value is used as identification of the lightbox (E.g. lightbox="myLightbox1" ). Component can be registered just in one Lightbox, so it is not possible to register a component for local and global Lighbox at the same time.

lightboxTrigger.description: Sets the mode in which the lightbox can be opened. Image - lightbox is opened by clicking on the image Button - lightbox is opened by clicking on the button in the right top corner

alt.description: The alt attribute is used to describe an image in case an image cannot be loaded (does not exist) or its loading is blocked by the user. Attribute content is also used by scanners for the blind and therefore it is suitable to describe image content with words. If object or function is passed, useLsi hook is used. E.g. alt="An image description"

aspectRatio.description: Property defines the aspect ratio of the image and could be one of defined values in AspectRatio . For the right use there has to be either width or height defined.

borderRadius.description: Border radius could be one of defined values in PropTypes .borderRadius. Example: borderRadius="expressive"

getSrc.description: Allows adjusting the src before it gets used, e.g. by retrieving and adding access key to it. The async function receives single parameter - current src , and it should return final URL to use. Example: getSrc={async (src) => createAuthorizedUrl(src, await getAccessKey(src))}

getThumbnailSrc.description: Allows adjusting the thumbnailSrc before it gets used, e.g. by retrieving and adding access key to it. The async function receives single parameter - current thumbnailSrc , and it should return final URL to use. Example: getThumbnailSrc={async (src) => createAuthorizedUrl(src, await getAccessKey(src))}

href.description: A url address to another visual use case or a position to some section. It can have the following forms: absolute url address link to web e.g. https://unicorn.com link to file e.g. blob:.. or file:... link to e-mail or phone e.g. mailto:... or tel:... fragment - a link to the component in the current visual use case, e.g. #form

target.description: Determines where a new page is opened: _blank - opens a new browser window, _parent - opens a page in the parent frame (in more complex frame structures), _top - opens a page in the full size window (not in a frame), _self - opens a page in the same frame or window. (default) custom name of the browser tab, where the new page is always open to. Example: target="_blank" or target="myTab"

thumbnailVariant.description: Defines type of image which is displayed: default - component selects image based on the available width: if the width is less than 300px, a smaller size is used; otherwise, the original size is displayed. small - component always displays small if thumbnail exists otherwise original image is used original - component always displays original image

description: @since 2.4.0 Component for cycling through images. It can display one or multiple images, that can be cycled through automatically by timer or manually by clicking on controll buttons.

initialIndex.description: Initial index of the active item. Example: initialIndex={3}

margin.description: The prop defines the size of the space around the component. Example: margin={8} or margin="8px" or margin="8px 16px" margin="8px 12px 16px" or margin="8px 12px 16px 18px"

intervalMs.description: Defines a time in milliseconds, after which the component will automatically move on to the next item. Example: intervalMs={8000}

stopIntervalOnHover.description: @since 1.15.0 When set to true , cycling through items will stop on hover.

colorScheme.description: Color of the component's control elements. Available values are defined in PropTypes . Example: colorScheme="primary"

contentHeight.description: Defines a height of the content part of the component (where the children are rendered). @since 1.23.0 If "auto" , component's height will be changing according to the height of the currently active item. Example: contentHeight={200} or contentHeight="200px"

type.description: Defines a behavior of the component after reaching the last item. Available values are: infinite - The component will cycle between the items in a circular fashion. final - After the last item, the component will stop moving forward (when interval is defined) and the button for moving forward will be disabled (when buttons is not "none" ). rewind - After the last item, the component will automatically rewind through all the items back to the beginning and continues forth. Example: stepper="inifinite"

stepper.description: Defines if and how should navigation stepper be displayed. Available values are: none - Not displayed inner - Absolutely positioned on top of the cycling items, not taking up any space. outer - Displayed outside the content wrapper of the component, besides the cycling items. Example: stepper="none"

buttons.description: Defines if and how should navigation buttons be displayed. Available values are: none - Not displayed inner - Absolutely positioned on top of the cycling items, not taking up any space. outer - Displayed outside the content wrapper of the component, besides the cycling items. Example: buttons="none"

animation.description: @since 1.25.0 Type of the animation. Example: animation="none" // for switch off the animation

virtualization.description: Determines whether the component will virtualize its items. Only the item that is currently displayed or the ones in the immediate vicinity will be rendered. Once the item is rendered, it will not unmount. Highly recommanded to define props.contentHeight for cases, when some items can have different height then virtualized items. Otherwise component can update its own size.

borderRadius.description: @since 1.16.0 Border radius could be one of defined values in PropTypes .borderRadius. Example: borderRadius="full"

id.description: Unified id of the component in uuUve. This value is set to the root html element to parameter id .

className.description: One or more class names separated by space. These class names are used in the root html element of the component in parameter class .

style.description: Styles are passed to the root html element of the component into parameter style .

disabled.description: If true, root html element of the component will contain parameter disabled. This element will be with opacity 0.4.

hidden.description: If true, root html element of the component will contain parameter hidden and this component will not be visibled.

elementRef.description: This property is set to root html element of the component to ref parameter. This is standard react behaviour .

elementAttrs.description: All html attributes which are supported by root html tag of the component and which are not in props.

noPrint.description: If true, whole component includes its children will not be printed

fullTextSearchPriority.description: If property is set to 0, the component and its children will not be indexed by fullTextSearch. If 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 is set, fullTextSearch will index it by this priority (1 - the lowest, 5 - the highest).

nestingLevel.description: Visual component, especially Brick component should have nesting level. This property set, which maximum nesting level of the component will be displayed in. Possible values: uve route areaCollection area boxCollection box spotCollection spot inline

itemMinWidth.description: Allows displaying multiple items if they fit within the carousel width; otherwise, the component attempts to fit as many items as possible within the available space. Example: itemMinWidth={300)

description: @since 2.4.0 This component is used only as a child of the Carousel component.

margin.description: The prop defines the size of the space around the component. Example: margin={8} or margin="8px" or margin="8px 16px" margin="8px 12px 16px" or margin="8px 12px 16px 18px"

loadingContent.description: This content is rendered while image is loading. Image component creates placeholder by passed width, height and aspectRatio and render loadingContent at the center of the placeholder.

thumbnailSrc.description: Url source of thumbnail image. Image from set url is displayed in the content and props.src is used and rendered only in the displayed lightbox.

fit.description: cover - the image is centered and shrinked to cover the whole area preserving its own aspect ratio, merely centered and possibly clipped in the other dimension if it overflows. contain - Image is centered and scaled to maintain its aspect ratio while fitting the area. @since 2.4.0 contain-background - Image is centered and scaled to maintain its aspect ratio while fitting the area and around the image is a blurred background filling the rest of the area . fill - The entire image will completely fill the box. If the object's aspect ratio does not match the aspect ratio of its box, then the object will be stretched to fit. To be able to use fit property, there has to be defined width and height property.

effect.description: Effect that shows on hover on thumbnail. Supported effects: none , zoom , grayscale , blur , invert , tilt , morph , sepia .

width.description: Required thumbnail image width (px). The second dimension is calculated to preserve the aspect ratios of the image.

height.description: Required thumbnail height (px). The second dimension is calculated to preserve the aspect ratios of the image.

lightbox.description: Lightbox is interface for displaying images with several functions as zoom, fullscreen, autoplay or browsing through the images with the same lightbox. Value can be bool, which sets if the component should be registered to the gobal lightbox (all components with lightbox={true} on the same page). The string value is used to register component to a local lightbox, where the value is used as identification of the lightbox (E.g. lightbox="myLightbox1" ). Component can be registered just in one Lightbox, so it is not possible to register a component for local and global Lighbox at the same time.

alt.description: The alt attribute is used to describe an image in case an image cannot be loaded (does not exist) or its loading is blocked by the user. Attribute content is also used by scanners for the blind and therefore it is suitable to describe image content with words. If object or function is passed, useLsi hook is used. E.g. alt="An image description"

aspectRatio.description: Property defines the aspect ratio of the image and could be one of defined values in AspectRatio . For the right use there has to be either width or height defined.

borderRadius.description: Border radius could be one of defined values in PropTypes .borderRadius. Example: borderRadius="expressive"

getSrc.description: Allows adjusting the src before it gets used, e.g. by retrieving and adding access key to it. The async function receives single parameter - current src , and it should return final URL to use. Example: getSrc={async (src) => createAuthorizedUrl(src, await getAccessKey(src))}

getThumbnailSrc.description: Allows adjusting the thumbnailSrc before it gets used, e.g. by retrieving and adding access key to it. The async function receives single parameter - current thumbnailSrc , and it should return final URL to use. Example: getThumbnailSrc={async (src) => createAuthorizedUrl(src, await getAccessKey(src))}

href.description: A url address to another visual use case or a position to some section. It can have the following forms: absolute url address link to web e.g. https://unicorn.com link to file e.g. blob:.. or file:... link to e-mail or phone e.g. mailto:... or tel:... fragment - a link to the component in the current visual use case, e.g. #form

target.description: Determines where a new page is opened: _blank - opens a new browser window, _parent - opens a page in the parent frame (in more complex frame structures), _top - opens a page in the full size window (not in a frame), _self - opens a page in the same frame or window. (default) custom name of the browser tab, where the new page is always open to. Example: target="_blank" or target="myTab"

thumbnailVariant.description: Defines type of image which is displayed: default - component selects image based on the available width: if the width is less than 300px, a smaller size is used; otherwise, the original size is displayed. small - component always displays small if thumbnail exists otherwise original image is used original - component always displays original image

lightboxTrigger.description: Sets the mode in which the lightbox can be opened. Image - lightbox is opened by clicking on the image Button - lightbox is opened by clicking on the button in the right top corner

description: @since 2.5.0 This component is used as an interface for displaying the source code.

margin.description: The prop defines the size of the space around the component. Example: margin=8 or margin="8px" or margin="8px 16px" margin="8px 12px 16px" or margin="8px 12px 16px 18px" margin="xs: 8px; m: 16px; l: 18px"

codeStyle.description: Language, based on which the editor highlights the content in color abap actionscript ada apache_conf assembly_x86 asm assembly batchfile bat batch msdos c_cpp c cpp c++ clojure cobol coffee coffeescript coldfusion csharp csharp c# cs css d dart diff dockerfile docker eiffel elm erlang forth fortran ftl gitignore golang go groovy haml handlebars haskell html html_ruby erb rhtml ini java javascript js json jsp jsx kotlin latex less lisp lua lucene makefile markdown mysql objectivec ocaml pascal perl pgsql php powershell prolog properties python r rdoc rhtml ruby rust sass scala scheme scss sh sql sqlserver svg swift tcl tex text typescript vbscript velocity xml yaml Example: codeStyle="css"

theme.description: Editor's theme chrome clouds crimson_editor dawn dreamweaver eclipse github iplastic solarized_light textmate tomorrow xcode kuroir katzenmilch sqlserver ambiance chaos clouds_midnight cobalt idle_fingers kr_theme merbivore merbivore_soft mono_industrial monokai pastel_on_dark solarized_dark terminal tomorrow_night tomorrow_night_blue tomorrow_night_bright tomorrow_night_eighties twilight vibrant_ink Example: theme="github"

fontSize.description: Font size in the editor. Example: fontSize="15px" or fontSize={18}

displayGutter.description: Shows row numbers and arrows for collapsing parts of the code on the left side of the editor. Example: displayGutter={false}

value.description: Code inserted in the editor. Example: value="<Uu5Elements.Button />"

borderRadius.description: Border radius could be one of defined values in Uu5.PropTypes .borderRadius. Example: borderRadius="expressive"

disabled.description: Editor is in the disabled mode. Example: disabled={false}

indent.description: Number of spaces used for line indentation clicking on Tab. Example: indent={15}

annotations.description: Allows you to add annotations to any line in the editor. Inputted as an array. Each annotation has its row and column. Example: annotations={[{ row:1, text: "informational text", type: "info"}]}

markers.description: List of lines/scope which should be highlighted. Each item of the array is of the object type and has the following attributes: startRow (number) – initial row (numbered from 1) startColumn (number) – initial column (numbered from 1) endRow (number) – final row endColumn (number) – final column colorScheme (string) – color schema used for highlighting. Only basic values are available from Uu5.PropTypes . Examples for creating marker are in the info block under the section with props.

wrapEnabled.description: If set to true, the editor wraps rows. Example: wrapEnabled={false}

minRows.description: Minimal number of rows in the editor. Example: minRows={20}

maxRows.description: Maximal number of rows in the editor. Example: maxRows={50}

description: The component is a block type component for which you can enable content editing. This component is used to edit text and inline components. The editor allows the user to use simple text formatting such as bold, italics, text and background color, etc. It is possible to work with paragraphs and lists.

uu5String.description: A property containing editor content in uu5String.

placeholder.description: Text, which is showed inside an empty editor.

readOnly.description: Specifies that an editor field is read-only, making it non-editable.

description: @since 5.0.0 User-oriented component for displaying and editing a tree nested item structure. Extends Uu5TreeElements.Tree with editing functionality like adding, modifying, or deleting items via editing mode.

itemList.description: List of items, which can contain nested itemList with the same structure. Structure of the item: header [node] - header of the item could be string or whatever inline component, children [node] - content under the header, actionList [object[]] - standard list of buttons (same structure as itemList in ActionGroup ), itemList [object[]] - nested items with the same structure (the nesting depth of items is not limited), expanded [bool] - it the item displays its nested items or not, selected [bool] - if true, the item and all of its parent will be selected, icon [string] - icon at the start of row, which is also displayed as collapsible button, onClick [func] - function is called when user click on the item, colorScheme [oneOf] - only colorScheme from building, meaning and basic is supported, significance [oneOf] - all significances are supported ( common , highlighted , distinct and subdued ), default is common .

size.type: xxs - xs - s - m - l - xl
size.description: Size defines minimal height of the item without its children. For compact mode use xxs .

height.description: If height is defined, then there is scrollbar if the content is higher.

itemColorScheme.description: All building , meaning and basic color schemes are available. Color scheme is default for each item in the tree. Example: itemColorScheme="primary" or itemColorScheme="pink"

itemSignificance.description: All significances as common , distinct and subdued are available. Significance is default for each item in the tree.

iconSignificance.description: Significance of icon button. It is possible to set: common subdued

expanded.description: Expand/collapse all items with item list.

margin.description: The prop defines the size of the space around the component. Example: margin=8 or margin="8px" or margin="8px 16px" margin="8px 12px 16px" or margin="8px 12px 16px 18px" margin="xs: 8px; m: 16px; l: 18px"

description: @since 2.2.0 The component is used for displaying animations.

autoPlay.description: If animation should play automaticaly, when it is loaded.

src.description: Source uri of the animation's JSON file. The component will attempt to load the data.

loop.description: If animation should continue from the start, when it ends.

width.description: Defines width of the animation.

height.description: Defines height of the animation.

showLoading.description: Whether to show loading indication (if using src prop).

description: @since 2.3.0 Animation of snake as an example of the animation concept.

position.description: From where the animation will start: left - snake is going from left to right, right - snake is going from right to left.

text.description: Text will be displayed in a callout.

textType.description: Type of the callout, where is text placed: speech thought

description: Component enhance Uu5Math.Expression with edit mode.

editMode.description: Standard editMode object provided by uuEcc library to allow run of edit mode.

expression.description: Mathematic expression which should be displayed by component.

description: @since 3.2.0 The XyChart is used to visualize the relationship between two variables. They are usually these variables recorded on the X-axis (horizontal) and Y-axis (vertical) and each point on graph represents one pair of values (X, Y). There are several types of XY charts such as point, line, column or area.

data.description: The prop has several settings. The simplest is an array of numbers that will be rendered in the chart so that the label is the order of the number (numbered from 1) and the value is the number: data={[20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70]} Another option is a table structure, or an array of fields, where each item is represented by an array with the first value specifying the label and the second specifying the measured value: data={[ ["John", "2000-02-20", ...], ... ]} The last option is an array of objects where each object contains a key and a value: data={[ { name: "John", dateOfBirth: "2000-02-20", ... }, ... ]}

serieList.description: An array of series, where each series is represented by an object with its own settings. Series can be visualized through different types of graphs. The common attributes of all the types are set directly in the series object, and the settings of the individual types are always under the given type. The types are the following: point , line , area , and bar . Each series can have a maximum of one type set, either as a boolean true or an object with the settings of the type. The descriptions of each setting can be found below. valueKey valueAxisId title colorScheme color onClick label unit point line area bar legend @since 3.1.0 Example: series={[ { valueKey: "count", bar: true }, { valueKey: "optimal", point: true }, { valueKey: "maximal", line: true }, ]}

labelAxis.description: This property contains a set of props to define the X axis. It is defined by an object containing the following props: dataKey [string - number]( required ) - key of data displayed in the axis title [string] - value of label which is rendered bellow the axis unit [string] - unit of data displayed in the axis tickList [array] @since 3.1.0 - array of ticks for labelAxis definition domain [string[] - number[] - func[]] @since 3.6.0 - allows to set minimal and maximal values on x-axis: "auto" - calculated automatically "dataMin"/"dataMax" - calculated from the minimum and maximum values formatValue [func] @since 3.6.0 - allows to format ticks on labelAxis Example: labelAxis={{ title: "Month", dataKey: "month" }}

valueAxis.description: Same as valueAxis in XYChart with additional props: round [number] @since 3.3.0 - coefficient, which divides value of the y-axis. domain [number[] - string[]] @since 3.3.0 - allows to set minimal and maximal values on y-axis. Available values are: any number e.g. [0, 10] auto e.g. [10, "auto"]

width.description: Can be set in any CSS unit.

height.description: Can be set in any CSS unit.

displayCartesianGrid.description: The prop displays the Cartesian grid. Example: displayCartesianGrid={true} @since 3.6.0 displayCartesianGrid="solid"

layout.description: The layout of areas, bars, lines in the chart. Example: layout="vertical"

lineList.description: Straight lines can be defined as arrays of objects, where each object represents a single line with the following setting: x [number - string] - the value of the X axis, which the line should pass through, it is set to 0 by default, y [number - string] - the value of the Y axis, which the line should pass through, it is set to 0 by default, x1 [number - string] @since 3.5.0 - the first value of the start of diagonal, x2 [number - string] @since 3.5.0 - the first value of the end of diagonal, y1 [number - string] @since 3.5.0 - the second value of the start of diagonal y2 [number - string] @since 3.5.0 - the second value of the end of diagonal title [string] - the title of the straight line or its label, titlePosition [oneOf] – the label position, can be start , middle or end , colorScheme [colorScheme] - the colorScheme of the straight line (it is ignored when color property is set), color [string] - the color of the straight line, width [number] - the width of the straight line in pixels, type ["solid" - "dashed" - "dotted"] @since 3.1.0 - the type of the line, isFront [bool] @since 3.1.0 - if set true, the line will be rendered in front of bars, lines, points, etc. Example: lineList={[ { y: 35, title: "Optimum", color: "green", titlePosition: "start" }, { x: "March", title: "Start", color: "orange" } ]}

tooltip.description: Display tooltip when hovering over data in the chart. This property can be defined with: [bool] - if true (default value), default Tooltip component is used. [element] - it is possible to use a Component to render custom Tooltip. [func] - the same as for the element, but instead of a Component, a function is used to render custom Tooltip Both [element] and [func] variants receive these props: label - X axis label serieList - an array of objects representing individual displayed values of the series for an item over which the mouse hovers. Each object contains the following information: title - series title valueKey - the key of the item in the data value - the value of the item in the data color - hex color of the series data - an object with an entire item in the data unit - the unit of the item in the data Example: { const { label, series } = props; return ( {series.map((item, i) => { const { color, title, value, unit } = item; return ( {title}: {value}{unit} ) })} ) }}" codeStyle="javascript" showGutter=false>

numberGroupingSeparator.description: A character separating thousands in the component's value labels. By default user preference settings is taken. Example: groupingSeparator=" " or groupingSeparator="," or groupingSeparator="."

numberDecimalSeparator.description: A character separating decimals in the component's value labels. By default user preference settings is taken. E.g. decimalSeparator="," or decimalSeparator="."

areaList.description: Areas can be defined as arrays of objects, where each object represents a single area with the following setting: x1 [number - string] - the X value of the lower left corner, x2 [number - string] - the X value of the upper right corner, y1 [number - string] - the Y value of the lower left corner y2 [number - string] - the Y value of the upper right corner title [string] - the title of the straight line or its label, titlePosition [oneOf] – the label position, can be start , middle or end , colorScheme [colorScheme] - the colorScheme of the straight line (it is ignored when color property is set), color [string] - the color of the straight line, isFront [bool] - if set true, the line will be rendered in front of bars, lines, points, etc. Example: areaList={[ { x1: "March", y1: 5, x2: "April", y2: 10, title: "Optimum", color: "green", titlePosition: "start" } ]}

dotList.description: Dots can be defined as arrays of objects, where each object represents a single dot with the following setting: x [number - string] - the value of the X axis, y [number - string] - the value of the Y axis, title [string] - the title of the straight line or its label, titlePosition [oneOf] – the label position, can be start , middle or end , colorScheme [colorScheme] - the colorScheme of the straight line (it is ignored when color property is set), color [string] - the color of the straight line, radius [number] - the radius of the point in pixels, isFront [bool] - if set true, the line will be rendered in front of bars, lines, points, etc. Example: pointList={[ { x: "March" y: 10, title: "Optimum", color: "green", titlePosition: "start" } ]}

legend.description: Legend could be switched on by bool value of defined by object: title [node] - the title of the legend position [oneOf] - the position relative to the graph. The available values are top , bottom , left , right Example: legend={true} or legend={{ title: "Legend", position: "bottom" }}

colorTheme.description: Default color theme for series. Example: colorTheme="contrast"

stackOffset.description: Only works for area and bar type charts with stackId . Defines, how the data are stacked for series with same stackId . By default this value is computed from data if the data values are numbers or not. Numbers are stacked as "sign", other data are stacked as "none". Sign stacks are rendered as two separate stacks. Negative values are rendered from zero y-axis down. Positive numbers are rendered from zero y-axis up. None stacks are rendered from the last point, where previous serie ends. So even positive values can be rendered below y-axis because it can be rendered from negative start. For set " none " value is recommanded to ensure, that all data in each serie are non-negative (positive or zero) or non-positive (negative or zero).

disableZoom.description: When set to true, disables user zoom on chart.

barStackGap.description: In BarChart , determines inner space between bars of the same category.

barGap.description: In BarChart, determines outer space between bars of different category.

zoomValue.description: An array of two numbers [start, end] defining the visible data range. For numeric data, values correspond to actual data values; for categorical data (strings), they represent data indices. The value is initial only. Use onZoomChange prop to make it fully controlled.

onZoomChange.description: Callback function called when zoom is changed. It receives an event where event.data is an object containing: zoomValue If this prop is used, prop zoomValue becomes controlled , i.e. it is expected that when onZoomChange is called, the parent component should store information passed to this function in its own state, and then pass that information back in the aforementioned props.

zoomType.description: Type of zoom with following options: button - After zooming in, a Reset button appears in the top-right corner of the chart. Clicking it restores the chart to its original view. brush - Renders a brush with interactive controls beneath the chart to adjust the zoom level. null - Disable zoom. E.g.: zoomType="brush" zoomType=null

description: @since 3.2.0 A PieChart is a circular graphical representation used to display the proportional distribution of data categories. The chart is divided into slices, where each slice represents a specific data category. The size of each slice corresponds to the proportion or percentage of the whole that the category represents. PieCharts are an effective way to visualize relative contributions or shares of different categories within a dataset. They offer a quick and easy-to-understand view of the overall composition or distribution of data.

data.description: Similar to XYChart , but for multiple series, the data is set as an array of data, or more precisely, an array of arrays. The number of data sets set in the array must be the same as the number of defined series. Example: data={[data, data2]}

serieList.description: Series are set similarly to XYChart . The main difference is that when displaying multiple series, each series can display a different set of data. So, for multiple series, the data is set as an array of data, where the item structure is the same as in XYChart. The number of defined series determines the number of data sets in an array. The Series has a definition similar to XYChart, but several settings are new. The descriptions of each setting can be found below. valueKey onClick label labelKey innerRadius outerRadius startAngle endAngle gap children colorScheme color unit Example: series={[ { valueKey: "sum", labelKey: "monthName" }, { valueKey: "value", labelKey: "name" } ]}

height.description: Can be set in any CSS unit.

The available values are top , bottom , left , right Example: legend={true} or legend={{ title: "Legend", position: "bottom" }}

colorTheme.description: Default color theme for series. Example: colorTheme="contrast"

description: @since 3.3.0 A RadarChart is a graphical representation used to visualize multivariate data across multiple attributes or variables. It consists of a central point and a series of data points connected by lines, forming a polygon shape. Each data point corresponds to a specific attribute, and the distance from the center of the chart to the data point reflects the value of that attribute. RadarCharts are useful for comparing and analyzing patterns, strengths, and weaknesses across different categories within a dataset.

serieList.description: An array of series, where each series is represented by an object with its own settings. Possible props for each series: valueKey [string - number]( required ) - defines the key under which values are entered in the props data, which will be displayed on radial axis. colorScheme [colorScheme] - the colorScheme of the series. It is ignored when color propery is set. color [string] - the color of the series. It is generated automatically if not set. It is possible to set it as a hex color or by the name of the color in English. title [node] - the title of the individual data item. It is mainly for displaying title of the data item in Tooltip and Legend.

labelAxis.description: The property is for defining the radial axis. It is defined by an object containing the following props: dataKey [string - number]( required ) - the key in the data displayed in the axis Example: labelAxis={{ dataKey: "productAttribute" }}

valueAxis.description: The property is for defining the radius axis. It is defined by an object containing the following props: angle [number] - defines angle of the radius axis. If set to null then radius axis is hidden Example: valueAxis={{ angle: 30 }}

startAngle.description: Defines an angle in degrees that indicates the start of the whole chart.

endAngle.description: Defines and angle in degrees that indicates the end of the whole chart.

innerRadius.description: The inner diameter of the chart. Setting it will cause the chart to not have a filled center. It can be set in pixels, numbers, or percentages as a string.

outerRadius.description: The outer diameter of the chart. It can be set in pixels, numbers, or percentages as a string.

description: @since 3.3.0 A RadialBarChart is a visual representation that displays data as a series of bars radiating from the center of the chart. Each bar corresponds to a data point, and its length is proportional to the value it represents. RadialBarCharts are particularly effective for showcasing the distribution or progression of values around a central point. They are often used to highlight relationships, trends, or comparisons within a dataset, providing a clear and intuitive way to convey complex information.

data.description: Data that defines details for displaying the chart. Connection between data and data series is done for each series separately via series property. description: @since 1.3.0 Uu5Elements.Modal , which wraps the embedded components and, if not in the home application, adds a visual identification of the application - a colored border on the left and an IdentificationIcon .

identificationType.description: The identification type. If "basic" , the identification is visually visible as a vertical stripe and an icon, if "none" , it is not visible. If undefined , the type is computed based on whether the component is in home application (effectively same as "none" ) or not ( "basic" ).

displayHelpCenter.description: Whether to display a help center action (button with question mark) in the action list of the component. Example: displayHelpCenter={false}

open.description: If modal should be displayed. Example: open={false}

onClose.description: Function is called when Modal is closed by close button, click on overlay or by ESC keyboard button. Example: onClose={event => setOpen(false)}

header.description: Header of the modal. Example: header="Add Item" header={<Lsi lsi={{ cs: "Přidat položku", en: "Add Item" }} />}

headerSeparator.description: Separator between header and content. Example: headerSeparator={false}

actionList.description: Similar to itemList in ActionGroup . Example: actionList={[ { icon: "uugds-favorites", tooltip: {en: "", ...} }, { icon: "uugds-plus", children: "Create", primary: true }, { icon: "uugds-reload", itemList: [{...}] } ]}

actionLeft.description: @since 1.9.0 Button or Dropdown props. colorScheme is by default set to "dim" significance is by default set to "subdued" Action will be displayed to the left of header content. Example: actionLeft={{ icon: "uugds-favorites", tooltip: {cs: "", en: ""}, onClick: () => ...}}

initialLeftOpen.description: @since 1.9.0 Determines if the left panel is visible from the start. If set to false, the user can open it via the hamburger icon next to the modal window's header.

leftWidth.description: @since 1.9.0 Width of the menu in pixels.

left.description: @since 1.9.0 A function that returns a content that is rendered in the left panel. Parameters: [object] parentPadding - {paddingLeft: unit, paddingRight: unit, paddingTop: unit, paddingBottom: unit} Example: left={({paddingLeft, paddingRight, paddingTop, paddingBottom}) => ( <Uu5Elements.ScrollableBox padding={{left: paddingLeft, right: paddingRight, top: paddingTop, bottom: paddingBottom}} > {...otherContent} </Uu5Elements.ScrollableBox> )}

footer.description: Any elements or @since 1.9.0 function, which will be in footer. There could be buttons but even some text. If a function is used, it should return content to render in footer. It receives an object containing: style [object] - style object containing paddingLeft , paddingTop , paddingRight , paddingBottom values to achieve standard look of the footer. Example: footer={<Uu5Elements.Button>Submit</Uu5Elements.Button>} footer={({ style }) => <div className={Css.css(style)}>...</div>} footer="footer content"

footerSeparator.description: Separator between content and footer. Example: footerSeparator={false}

initialDisplayInfo.description: @since 1.10.0 If true , Modal is displayed with open info. @depreceated 1.16.0 Info is diplayed inside new Popover component which is always hidden on initial render.

width.description: Width of the modal. For full screen use "full" , for adaptation to content, use null . Example: width="full" or width={null} or width={720} or width="20em"

fullscreen.description: If true , modal is displayed for whole viewport.

borderRadius.description: Border radius could be one of defined values in PropTypes .borderRadius except full . Example: borderRadius="expressive"

scrollable.description: Defines whether modal's content can be scrollable or not.

closeOnEsc.description: Modal will be closed if ESC keyboard button is pressed.

closeOnOverlayClick.description: Modal will be closed if click on overlay in background is happen.

closeOnButtonClick.description: Button with cross is displayed in the top right side of the Modal.

collapsible.description: @since 1.19.0 If true , the content will be collapsible and the Modal will contain a button for collapsing.

skipModalBus.description: If true , modal is not displayed in ModalBus .

lsi.description: @since 1.11.0 Override of default lsi values. Object with one or more items, each having language keys with localized values. uu5 uses ISO-639-1 Language Codes and ISO-3166 Alpha-2 Country Codes with downcases syntax. Example: lsi = {{ moreInfo: { en: "More Details" } }}

children.description: If a function is used, it receives an object containing paddings. In this case modal does not have a padding and it must be somehow used in rendered content as in example. style [object] - style object containing paddingLeft , paddingTop , paddingRight , paddingBottom values to achieve standard look. Example: {({ style }) => <div className={Css.css(style)}>...</div>}

leftOpen.description: leftOpen determines whether the drawer is open/close. The value is initial only when is used without onLeftChange prop. Also this property override initialLeftOpen .

onLeftChange.description: A function called when drawer state is changed. It receives and event where event.data is an object containing open . If this prop is used, prop leftOpen becomes controlled , i.e. it is expected that when onLeftChange is called, the parent component should store information passed to onLeftChange function in its own state, and then pass that information back in the aforementioned props.

colorScheme.description: Color of the text define semantic sense throughout the information hierarchy. Available values are defined in PropTypes . Example: colorScheme="primary"

significance.description: Significance differentiates text according to its visibility or visual expression throughout the interface. Available values are: common , highlighted , distinct , subdued . Example: significance="highlighted"

restrainedHeader.description: Makes header restrained, i.e. value in prop header is not shown (it is, however, shown in ModalBus when this modal is temporarily deactivated or in a dropdown for switching among modals when there're >=4 modals opened) but actions in actionList and closing button are shown. The developer must lay out the modal content carefully so that actions do not overlap the content in a weird way.

id.description: Unified id of the component in uuUve. This value is set to the root html element to parameter id .

className.description: One or more class names separated by space. These class names are used in the root html element of the component in parameter class .

style.description: Styles are passed to the root html element of the component into parameter style .

disabled.description: If true, root html element of the component will contain parameter disabled. This element will be with opacity 0.4.

hidden.description: If true, root html element of the component will contain parameter hidden and this component will not be visibled.

elementRef.description: This property is set to root html element of the component to ref parameter. This is standard react behaviour .

elementAttrs.description: All html attributes which are supported by root html tag of the component and which are not in props.

noPrint.description: If true, whole component includes its children will not be printed

fullTextSearchPriority.description: If property is set to 0, the component and its children will not be indexed by fullTextSearch. If 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 is set, fullTextSearch will index it by this priority (1 - the lowest, 5 - the highest).

nestingLevel.description: Visual component, especially Brick component should have nesting level. This property set, which maximum nesting level of the component will be displayed in. Possible values: uve route areaCollection area boxCollection box spotCollection spot inline

info.description: Description of the component, which is created by the Block. Text can contain links . If info as object is set, it can contains: help [node] - custom info about the content of the component, fls [object] @since 1.27.0 baseUri [string] - baseUri to uuFls, where will be send requests according to the content of the component, tagList [string[]] - list of tags which must be supported in used uuFls awid, topic [string] - topic which must be supported in used uuFls awid. sls [object] @since 1.27.0 baseUri [string] - baseUri to uuSls, where will be send requests according to the content of the component, tagList [string[]] - list of tags which must be supported in used uuSls awid, topic [string] - topic which must be supported in used uuSls awid. uu5Tag [string] - @since 1.26.0 uu5Tag of the component, which the info belongs to, actionList [object[]] - @since 1.26.0 array of button's props. It is possible to set custom button component by { component: MyComponent } displayAwidAbout [bool-object] - @since 1.37.0 if set, AwidAbout button is displayed in Help tab in Help center if help is also set. If it is necessary to change default label for the button, it could be done as object with key label as node. E.g. displayAwidAbout={true} or displayAwidAbout={{ label: "About AWID" }} or displayAwidAbout={{ label: <Lsi ... /> }} displayAsidAbout [bool-object] - @since 1.37.0 if set, AsidAbout button is displayed in Advanced tab in Help center. If it is necessary to change default label for the button, it could be done as object with key label as node. E.g. displayAsidAbout={true} or displayAsidAbout={{ label: "About ASID" }} or displayAsidAbout={{ label: <Lsi ... /> }} flsBaseUri [string] - @since 1.21.0 @deprecated 1.27.0 baseUri to uuFls, where will be send requests according to the content of the component, slsBaseUri [string] - @since 1.21.0 @deprecated 1.27.0 baseUri to uuSls, where will be send requests according to the content of the component, Example: info={{ help: <Lsi lsi={{ cs: "...", en: "..." }} />, fls: { baseUri: "https://uuapp.plus4u.net/..." }, sls: { baseUri: "https://uuapp.plus4u.net/..." }, uu5Tag: "UuFinmanBricks.BalanceSummary", actionList: [ { children: <Lsi lsi={{ en: "Permission settings", cs: "Nastavení práv" }}, onClick: () => ... }, { component: StateHistoryButton }, { component: <RelationsButton oid="abc123" /> }, ] }}

uuIdentity.description: The uuIdentity of the person, whose information is displayed. If property is not set, actual logged in person is displayed. Example: uuIdentity="7-7948-1"

imageSrc.description: Source of image which will be displayed as circle. Only one of icon , iconText or imageSrc can be set. @since 1.36.0 If imageSrc is set to null , than the photo is not displayed. Example: imageSrc="https://cnd.plus4u.net/..." imageSrc={null}

icon.description: Icon name with prefix of icon library. Only one of icon , iconText or imageSrc can be set. E.g. icon="uugds-favorites" or icon="uugdsstencil-it-react"

iconText.description: Initials or one or two characters which will be displayed instead of icon. Only one of icon , iconText or imageSrc can be set. Examples: iconText="UU"

title.description: Title of the component which is highlighted.

subtitle.description: Subtitle of the component with additional info.

size.type: xxs-xs-s-m-l-xl
size.description: Visual size of the component. Example: size="xl"

colorScheme.description: Color of the text define semantic sense throughout the information hierarchy. All values are available from PropTypes .colorScheme. It is only applied to the icon and the iconText . Example: colorScheme="primary"

significance.description: Significance differentiates text according to its visibility or visual expression throughout the interface. Available values are: common , highlighted , subdued . It is only applied to the icon and the iconText . Example: significance="highlighted"

direction.description: Visual composition of title and subtitle . horizontal - title and subtitle are placed side by side, vertical - title is located above subtitle , vertical-reverse - subtitle is located above title , vertical-full - @since 1.35.0 title is located below the icon and above the subtitle .

onClick.description: Function which is invoked after click or touch on the button. Parameters: [object] event - standard click attributes . Example: onClick={event => alert("onClick")}

tooltip.description: Tooltip is shown when the mouse is over the button or if you keep pressing the button on a mobile. It could be set as string or as lsi object. Example: tooltip="User detail" tooltip={{cs: "Detail uživatele", en: "User detail"}}

background.description: @deprecated 1.7.0 Deprecated - background is now found out automatically. In special cases, e.g. when there is light/dark image on the background, you can nest the component into BackgroundProvider and use its background prop. Background of the component which text component is placed on. Available values are: light , dark , full , soft . Example: background="full"

iconAnimation.description: Defines the animation of the icon. rotate - Applies rotating animation. none - Turns off the animation. Example: iconAnimation="rotate"

href.description: A url address to another visual use case or a position to some section. It can have the following forms: absolute url address link to web e.g. https://unicorn.com link to file e.g. blob:.. or file:... link to e-mail or phone e.g. mailto:... or tel:... relative url address e.g. /about.html or /about fragment - a link to the component in the current visual use case, e.g. #form uu5Route - a name of uu5Route which can contains parameters e.g. book or book/page?code=1234

target.description: Determines where a new page is opened: _blank - opens a new browser window, _parent - opens a page in the parent frame (in more complex frame structures), _top - opens a page in the full size window (not in a frame), _self - opens a page in the same frame or window. custom name of the browser tab, where the new page is always open to. By default is target="_blank" if href has another baseUri then current uuApp. Example: target="_blank" or target="myTab"

subtitle.description: The subtitle describing additional information about the error. Example: subtitle="Info about error" subtitle={{en: "Info about error", cs: "Informace o chybě"}} subtitle={<Lsi lsi={ { en: "Info about error", cs: "Informace o chybě" } } />}

It also adds common functionalities such as Copy component, Reload data, possibility to display the component as a modal, waiting for related data object(s) with possibility to specify custom error messages if they fail to load, and more.

title.description: Title of the component. It can also be an object containing nesting levels as keys and the value to show in case of that nesting level (or bigger nesting level). Example: title="Joke" title={{ box: "Joke", inline: "Show joke" }}

subtitle.description: Subtitle of the component. It can also be an object containing nesting levels as keys and the value to show in case of that nesting level (or bigger nesting level). Example: subtitle="uuJoke" subtitle={{ box: "uuJoke", inline: "(opens modal)" }}

displayAsModal.description: If true , displays the content in a modal.

onClose.description: Function is called when Modal is closed by close button, click on overlay or by ESC keyboard button. @since 1.38.0 When defined, a Close button is shown in area and route nesting level visualizations. Example: onClose={event => setOpen(false)}

getCopyOptions.description: If provided, the component will add "Copy component" action to the action list. When action is triggerred, function is called with no parameters and it must return an item or an array of items to copy. When user then attempts to paste the content, they will have option to choose from available items. Each item can contain: uu5Tag [string] - uu5Tag to copy props [object] - props to copy. name [string] - required if more items are used. The name of this variant for "Paste as" dialog. E.g. "Standard component" or "Link to component". desc [string] - optional description for this item in the dialog. icon [string] - optional icon. See actionList[].icon in Dialog . significance [string] - optional significance. See actionList[].significance in Dialog . colorScheme [string] - optional colorScheme. See actionList[].colorScheme in Dialog . Example: getCopyOptions={() => ({ uu5Tag: "UuDemo.Component", props: { baseUri, oid: JOKES[0].oid } })} or getCopyOptions={() => [ { name: "Standard component", uu5Tag: "UuDemo.Component", props: { baseUri, oid: JOKES[0].oid }, { name: "Link", uu5Tag: "UuDemo.Component", props: { baseUri, oid: JOKES[0].oid, nestingLevel: "inline" } ]}

getRedirectUri.description: Function for obtaining URL to navigate to if user attempts to open then component in a new tab, e.g. by middle-clicking on inline view. The function receives no parameters and should return URL string. If not given but getCopyOptions is given, component will be opened via default Plus4UGo uuApp using uu5Tag and props as returned from getCopyOptions . If getCopyOptions is not given either, opening does nothing. Example: getRedirectUri={() => Plus4U5.Utils.Uri.join(baseUri, "jokes", { oid: JOKES[0].oid })}

card.description: Card type of the view: none - there is not shadow, text starts from the left side of the component, full - box with shadow is around whole component, header, content and footer have same padding, content - box with shadow is only around the content and footer, header does not have a padding. Example: card="full"

aspectRatio.description: Aspect ratio for width and height in syntax <width>x<height> . All sizes are defined in uuGds as Box. Example: aspectRatio="16x9" or aspectRatio="4x3"

width.description: Width of the box. It could be set in all possible units. Default unit is px . Combination of aspectRatio and width is possible to keep standard height. Example: width={80} or width="50%" or width="8em"

colorScheme.description: Color of the text define semantic sense throughout the information hierarchy. Available values are defined in PropTypes as building , meaning and basic colors. Example: colorScheme="primary"

significance.description: Significance differentiates text according to its visibility or visual expression throughout the interface. Available values are: common , highlighted , distinct , subdued . Example: significance="highlighted"

displayType.description: The default display type for nesting level "spot". Example: displayType="button"

icon.description: The icon to use for nesting level "spot". Example: icon="uugdsstencil-home-lightbulb-glow"

open.description: In case that displayAsModal=true , decides whether the modal should be opened. If not given, behaves as true for backward compatibility. Example: open={true}

detailTarget.description: The property specifies how the component should be opened if its nestingLevel is set to inline. Possible options: modal - open component in modal (default behaviour) route - redirect user using getRedirectUri. If getRedirectUri is not filled home-go behaviour is used. home-go - redirect user to go route in destination app. local-go - re-route user to go route in current app. plus4u-go - open component in Plus4UGo . detail - @since 1.38.0 - open component as detail in global side detail layout . custom route - can be any URL function - @since 1.38.0 nothing is opened and the function is called with an event parameter containing newTab boolean. When it is true the detail should be opened to the new browser tab.

detailNewTabTarget.description: The property specifies how the component should be opened (in new tab window) if its nestingLevel is set to inline. Possible options: route - redirect user using getRedirectUri. If getRedirectUri is not filled home-go behaviour is used. home-go - redirect user to go route in destination app. local-go - re-route user to go route in current app. plus4u-go - open component in Plus4UGo . custom route - can be any URL function - @since 1.38.0 nothing is opened and the function is called

identificationType.description: The identification type. If "basic" , the identification is visually visible as a vertical stripe and an icon, if "none" , it is not visible. If undefined , the type is computed based on whether the component is in home application (effectively same as "none" ) or not ( "basic" ).

level.description: Level is used only for headerType="heading" . Level could be set or it is automatically calculated by level approach.

height.description: The height of the component. Value "auto" means that the component will be sized by the parent (e.g. CSS flex / grid) and should be scrollable. Note that if height is given and is different than "auto" , props minHeight and maxHeight are ignored. Example: height={200} or height="100%"

minHeight.description: The minimal height of the component. See also height . Example: minHeight={200}

maxHeight.description: The maximal height of the component. See also height . Example: maxHeight={200} or maxHeight="100%"

borderRadius.description: Border radius could be one of defined values in PropTypes .borderRadius except full . Example: borderRadius="expressive"

description: @since 1.28.0 The component shows pending indication while passed data object(s) is loading and after it's ready it renders its children (or an error if a data object(s) failed to load).

dataObject.description: A data object to wait for, or an array of these. The data object is an object coming from useDataObject / useDataList hooks.

lsiError.description: Lsi containing map with error messages depending on error codes / HTTP statuses. See useAlertBus main example for the list of error codes and keys that are recognized by default. Unrecognized errors will fall back to displaying default messages. @since 1.35.0 Lsi keys can contain * character(s) which match any sequence of characters. Example: lsiError={{ import, path: ["Errors"] }} where e.g. en.json can contain: "Errors": { "uu-joke/joke/jokeNotFound": "Joke does not exist or it was removed before.", "uu-joke/joke/*": "Operation on joke failed.", "unauthorized": "You don't have sufficient rights to do that." }

displayPending.description: Allows to disable internal pending resolver. When set to false, all pending states will behave as if the component is in a ready state. In this mode, the application or parent component should handle any pending states explicitly.

description: @since 1.28.0 A standard layout component for routes - it contains a header with action list, content, and a footer.

header.description: Header of the route. Example: header="Joke list"

footer.description: The content for the footer. Example: footer={<BackToTopButton />}

actionList.description: Menu with application controls. Structure is same as itemList in Uu5Element.ActionGroup . description: @since 1.33.0 Uu5Elements.Tile , which wraps the embedded components and, if not in the home application, adds a visual identification of the application - a colored border on the left and an IdentificationIcon .

identificationType.description: The identification type. If "basic" , the identification is visually visible as a vertical stripe and an icon, if "none" , it is not visible. If undefined , the type is computed based on whether the component is in home application (effectively same as "none" ) or not ( "basic" ).

actionList.description: Allows to render an ActionGroup on the right side of the Tile. The value can be the same as itemList in the ActionGroup .

displayActionList.description: Allow to control ActionGroup appearence behaviour on the top right side of the Tile. If undefined the ActionGroup becomes visible on hover (except mobile devices). headerOverlap.description: If false is set, the content of the header is displayed at the top of the Tile and the content in the Tile's children is below the header. headerSignificance.description: This prop sets significance only in Tile's header. Available values are: common , highlighted . Example: headerSignificance="highlighted"

headerColorScheme.description: This prop sets colorScheme only in Tile's header. Available values are same as colorScheme in Box . If the headerOverlap prop is enabled, the headerColorScheme prop has no effect on the display . Example: colorScheme="primary"

headerSeparator.description: @since 1.16.0 Shows line separator between header and body.

footer.description: The content of props footer is displayed at the bottom of the Tile. The footer can be string , number , component etc. Example: footer="Custom footer" or footer={2022} footer={<Uu5Elements.Link href="url">Footer</Uu5Elements.Link>}

footerOverlap.description: If false is set, the content of the footer is displayed at the bottom of the Tile and the content in the Tile's children is over the footer. colorScheme.description: Color of the text define semantic sense throughout the information hierarchy. Available values are defined in PropTypes as building , meaning and basic colors. Example: colorScheme="primary"

significance.description: Significance differentiates text according to its visibility or visual expression throughout the interface. Available values are: common , highlighted , distinct , subdued . Example: significance="highlighted"

footerSeparator.description: @since 1.16.0 Shows line separator between footer and body.

getCopyOptions.description: If provided, the component will add "Copy component" action to the action list. When action is triggerred, function is called with no parameters and it must return an item or an array of items to copy. When user then attempts to paste the content, they will have option to choose from available items. Each item can contain: uu5Tag [string] - uu5Tag to copy props [object] - props to copy. name [string] - required if more items are used. The name of this variant for "Paste as" dialog. E.g. "Standard component" or "Link to component". desc [string] - optional description for this item in the dialog. icon [string] - optional icon. See actionList[].icon in Dialog . significance [string] - optional significance. See actionList[].significance in Dialog . colorScheme [string] - optional colorScheme. See actionList[].colorScheme in Dialog . Example: getCopyOptions={() => ({ uu5Tag: "UuDemo.Component", props: { baseUri, oid: JOKES[0].oid } })} or getCopyOptions={() => [ { name: "Standard component", uu5Tag: "UuDemo.Component", props: { baseUri, oid: JOKES[0].oid }, { name: "Link", uu5Tag: "UuDemo.Component", props: { baseUri, oid: JOKES[0].oid, nestingLevel: "inline" } ]}

getRedirectUri.description: Function for obtaining URL to navigate to if user attempts to open then component in a new tab, e.g. by middle-clicking on inline view. The function receives no parameters and should return URL string. If not given but getCopyOptions is given, component will be opened via default Plus4UGo uuApp using uu5Tag and props as returned from getCopyOptions . If getCopyOptions is not given either, opening does nothing. Example: getRedirectUri={() => Plus4U5.Utils.Uri.join(baseUri, "jokes", { oid: JOKES[0].oid })}
